name: Stepwell Cafe
why_it_matters: Open-air rooftop cafe overlooking Toorji ka Jhalra — the 1740s stepwell built by Maharaja Abhaya Singh's queen and re-excavated in the 2010s after a century buried. Stone-and-wood interior, Mehrangarh Fort framed across the rooftops at dusk.
insider_tip: Sit on the side that looks down into the stepwell, not at the fort — the angle locals photograph is the carved sandstone steps below, which most visitors miss. Wood-fired pizzas are 20 minutes; order on arrival.
signature_address: Makrana Mohalla, Gulab Sagar, near Toorji ka Jhalra, Jodhpur 342001

name: Indique
why_it_matters: Top terrace of Pal Haveli — the only Jodhpur rooftop with line-of-sight to Mehrangarh Fort, Umaid Bhawan, Jaswant Thada, the Clock Tower, and Gulab Sagar all at once. Two levels: Indique on top, the lower Daudi (former zenana courtyard) as the bar.
insider_tip: Book the 6:30pm slot — fort lights come on around 7pm and Mehrangarh glows for the rest of the meal. Daudi (lower) is the move if you want cocktails-first.
signature_address: Pal Haveli, opposite Clock Tower, near Gulab Sagar, Jodhpur 342001

name: Shri Mishrilal Hotel
why_it_matters: Started 1927 by Mishrilal under a British government licence selling rabri, ghee kachori and koftas. In 1960 his son Radheyshyam developed Makhaniya Lassi — highly compressed curd with cardamom, kewda, sugar and milk — now Jodhpur's most cited sweet drink, served from the same hole-in-the-wall under Ghantaghar.
insider_tip: The shop is on the Ghantaghar (Clock Tower) side of Sardar Market — easy to miss because the signboard is in Hindi. Makhaniya lassi is finished with malai by hand; eat with a spoon, not a straw.
signature_address: Sardar Market, Girdikot, near Clock Tower, Jodhpur 342001

name: Janta Sweet Home
why_it_matters: Established 1980 on Nai Sarak — the city's reference shop for mawa kachori (a Jodhpur invention: kachori shell stuffed with khoya, almonds, pistachios, cardamom). Onion kachori and ghevar from the same counter; namkeen from a separate weighing table.
insider_tip: Mawa kachori must be eaten in-store, hot — packed boxes lose the flake within hours. The shop sits opposite Priya Hotel; mind the Nai Sarak scooter traffic.
signature_address: House No. 3, opposite Priya Hotel, near National Handloom, Nai Sarak, Jodhpur 342001

name: Shahi Samosa
signature_dish: shahi samosa with dry-fruit potato filling
why_it_matters: Anand Prakash Arora started frying samosas in 1984, adding dry fruits to the mashed-potato filling — the 'shahi' (royal) twist that gave the shop its name. The team still sets up one giant kadhai on Nai Sarak and turns out roughly 2,000 samosas a day.
insider_tip: Cash only; ₹20 per samosa. Eat with their tamarind chutney from the side counter, not the green chutney — the tangier tamarind is what cuts the dry-fruit filling.
signature_address: Shop No. 95/B, Clock Tower Road, Nai Sarak, Jodhpur 342001

name: Jhankar Choti Haveli
why_it_matters: Old-city pure-veg restaurant near Toorji's Stepwell, 5 minutes from Clock Tower. Rooftop terrace facing Mehrangarh Fort directly; the city's most-cited budget alternative to Indique for the same fort view.
insider_tip: Walk-in works for lunch; dinner needs a call ahead in season. The Marwari thali is unlimited — pace the dal baati churma, which fills you up faster than you think.
signature_address: Makrana Mohalla, Umed Chowk, behind Clock Tower, near Toorji ka Jhalra, Jodhpur 342001
